title: Paystride Payroll-Repaid Loan Training Notes: Earned Wage Access Balances and Write-offs in Loan Decisions
content:
**The rule.** Holding a Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan changes Paystride Payroll-Repaid Loan eligibility: an application is declined when the worker's access outstanding balance exceeds the loan tier's Earned Wage Access balance limit, or when an access write-off was booked within the tier's write-off look-back period of calendar days. While a loan is in repayment, the Access plan's combined deduction ceiling counts its installments, under the Access charter.

These training notes answer the questions the rule settles.

**What is the access outstanding balance?**
It is the total of the outstanding balances across all of the worker's Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan plans, taken as they stand at the application. A worker with more than one plan has all of them added together.

**When does the balance decline the application?**
Only when that total is more than the tier's limit. A total exactly equal to the limit does not exceed it, and the balance test does not decline the application.

**Which write-offs count?**
Access write-off entries booked on any of the worker's Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan plans in the look-back period, which is the stated number of calendar days before the application date. One such write-off in that period is enough to decline the application.

**Are the two tests alternatives?**
Yes. Either one on its own declines the application: a balance above the limit with no recent write-off, or a recent write-off with a balance under the limit.

**What happens on the Access side while the loan is repaid?**
While the loan is in repayment, its installments count toward the Access plan's combined deduction ceiling. That ceiling, and how it is applied, belongs to the Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan's own charter.

### Hypothetical screen

The figures below are hypothetical; the limit used is whatever limit the tier sets.

| Plans and outstanding balances | Total | Hypothetical tier limit | Write-off in the look-back period | Declined under this rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| one plan, $90.00 | $90.00 | $150.00 | none | No |
| two plans, $90.00 and $70.00 | $160.00 | $150.00 | none | Yes, balance above the limit |
| one plan, $150.00 | $150.00 | $150.00 | none | No, equal is not above |
| one plan, $20.00 | $20.00 | $150.00 | one | Yes, recent write-off |
